description:
The depth-suite trains every install as LoRA (Tinker). The LessWrong robust-model-organisms post finds training METHOD dominates robustness (FWFT > high-rank > low-rank LoRA). Central Q: is SDF's fragility about depth (docs vs QA) or an artifact of low-rank LoRA? Grid {LoRA-r8/r64/r256, FWFT} x {SDF docs, QA-SFT} at matched B(0), ED belief, Qwen3-14B (>=7B floor=8B), 3 seeds; primary stressor untargeted benign FT; Pareto everywhere. SINGLE training stack = Unsloth on one B200 (192GB) driven by bellhop (LoRA any rank + FWFT via full_finetuning=True) so method isn't confounded by stack; aligne only for data-gen, scimt.eval/match for eval+selection. Spec: experiments/lora_artifact_robustness/spec.md. H1 method dominates; H2 depth washes out under method control; H3 prompted floor.

## Notes
First-pass DONE + published (sci-mt #132, lab-notes #6, report 'Increasing LoRA rank improves robustness to benign finetuning'). Headline: robustness is a rank/LR/optimization story, not a depth fact. Remaining follow-ups: seeds (top gap), matched-install-LR FWFT, adversarial-FT (.7), prompted floor (.8), 30B confirm (.9).
title: Epic: is SDF's fragility a LoRA artifact? — method-controlled robustness (follow-up to GH#111)
